definition: Vicuna LLM is an omnibus large language model used in AI research.
details: Its methodology is to enable the public at large to contrast and compare the accuracy of LLMs "in the wild" (an example of citizen science) and to vote on their output; a question-and-answer chat format is used. At the beginning of each round two LLM chatbots from a diverse pool of nine are presented randomly and anonymously, their identities only being revealed upon voting on their answers. The user has the option of either replaying ("regenerating") a round, or beginning an entirely fresh one with new LLMs. (The user also has the option of choosing which LLMs to do battle.) Based on Llama 2, it is an open source project, and it itself has become the subject of academic research in the burgeoning field. A non-commercial, public demo of the Vicuna-13b model is available to access using LMSYS.

explainer.lead: Vicuna LLM is an omnibus large language model used in AI research. Its methodology is citizen science: letting the public contrast and compare LLM accuracy "in the wild" and vote on outputs.

tiers.eli5: Two chatbots answer your question without saying who they are, you pick the better answer, and only then are their names revealed.
tiers.practitioner: Each round randomly and anonymously presents two chatbots drawn from a diverse pool of nine in a question-and-answer chat format, with identities revealed only after voting. Users can replay ("regenerate") a round or start a fresh one; the pitfall is that judgments rest on anonymous public preference votes.
tiers.paperLevel: An omnibus LLM evaluated through blinded pairwise public voting: two of nine chatbots are shown anonymously per round in a Q&A chat format, identities revealed on vote, with rounds replayed or restarted at the user's option. Accuracy claims depend on crowd voting rather than controlled benchmarks.

explainer.example: A user asks a question, gets two anonymous answers from the pool of nine, votes for the better one, and only then sees which models produced them.
